definition: The rate at which a component transfers electrical energy to other forms, such as thermal energy in a resistor: $P = IV = I^2R = \frac{V^2}{R}$, measured in watts.
The resistance of the materials inside a cell; the current in the cell dissipates energy in it, so the terminal potential difference is $V = \varepsilon - Ir$.
The potential difference across a cell's terminals while it delivers a current; it is less than the emf by $Ir$, and equals the emf only when no current flows.
A resistor whose resistance changes a lot with temperature; in an NTC thermistor the resistance decreases as the temperature increases.
A resistor (LDR) whose resistance decreases as the intensity of the light falling on it increases.
